unit: % of nominal voltage lost (100 minus worst-phase retained voltage at the POI)
evidence_note: 15 distinct retained-voltage values from Texas large-load events (0.305 to 0.844 pu) converted to depth; median retained 0.486 pu. Readings of 0.00 pu (loss of supply, not a sag) are excluded
notes: Depth is my conversion; the retained values were re-checked against slides 8-9. Basis is worst phase; slide 9 shows positive-sequence dips much shallower, so choose the simulator's basis before use. Hunt search bounds may extend beyond the observed 15.6-69.5 up to 100
population: ERCOT reportable large-load events (skewed toward events that reduced load)
reverified: confirmed (retained values on slides 8-9); depth is a conversion

evidence_note: Normal clearing in 3 to 4 cycles (mean 3.3 cycles over 15 events), about 10 cycles after a breaker misoperation, 19 cycles after a breaker failure; converted at 60 Hz
notes: Typical is the mean of the 15 normal-clearing values tallied from slides 5, 8 and 9. NERC crypto report (about 5 cycles = 83 ms) is inside the range. NON-TEXAS comparison: 42-66 ms (Eastern Interconnection). Dropped: 20 ms (a threshold in the NERC report) and 0.9 cycles (relay operating time); neither is a clearing time
population: ERCOT reportable large-load events (skewed toward events that reduced load)
reverified: confirmed (cycles on slides 4, 5, 8, 9); mean is a tally

evidence_note: Six voltage depressions in about 82 s on one 230 kV line in the Eastern Interconnection: an arrestor failure followed by repeated auto-reclose attempts. ERCOT deck reports multiple 3LG faults within one minute at one West Texas 345 kV station, without a count
notes: NON-TEXAS for the high of 6. Typical of 1 is an assumption (Texas counts are not tabulated). The 6 are reclose attempts onto one persistent fault, not six independent faults
population: Single Eastern Interconnection event (high); Texas counts not tabulated
reverified: partly confirmed (NERC Table 1); typical is an assumption

evidence_note: Gaps between the six logged depressions computed from start times: 0.53, 15.3, 5.4, 55.0 and 5.4 s
notes: NON-TEXAS: Eastern Interconnection. Gaps are auto-reclose delays set by protection logic, not independent fault spacing. Typical 5.4 s is the median of the 5 gaps. ERCOT deck only says several faults fell within one minute
population: Single Eastern Interconnection event
reverified: confirmed (NERC Table 1 start times); median is a calculation

source_type: mixed: ERCOT forecast, LBNL, Microsoft ASPLOS, UK UPS sample
page_or_table: ERCOT 2025 LTLF p. 9; LBNL p. 6; ASPLOS Table 4; theenergyst article
evidence_note: Typical 0.50: ERCOT reports data centers in service 2022-2024 averaged 49.8% of requested MW at peak, and LBNL assumes 50% average utilization. High 0.97: peak share of provisioned power for training clusters (row level, normalized). Low 0.20: in a UK sample of 2,268 UPS, about 25% ran at 20% load or less.
notes: Modeling range built from sources on different bases (requested MW, utilization, provisioned power, UPS load); not a measurement of load at event start. Batch 2 left low and typical blank. Inference clusters peaked at 0.79. ERCOT's factor was measured on data centers and applied to non-crypto additions.
population: mixed; see evidence_note
reverified: confirmed (ERCOT 49.8% p. 9, LBNL 50% p. 6, ASPLOS 97% / 79%, Riello 25% at or below 20%)

unit: fraction of provisioned power (largest 2 s spike)
evidence_note: In production clusters the largest power jump in a 2-second window was 9% of provisioned power for inference and 37.5% for training.
notes: Typical is the midpoint (filled; the source gives no typical). The 2-second spike is a proxy for swing amplitude (label inferred). Values are row level and normalized for confidentiality. Region not stated.
population: one large US cloud operator, row/cluster level, DGX-A100-class
reverified: confirmed (Table 4: 37.5% and 9%)

evidence_note: Spectral energy of one measured at-scale training power trace on DGX-H100 racks is concentrated between 0.2 and 3 Hz.
notes: Typical is the midpoint (filled); the source gives a band, not a distribution. The band covers one training job. The factor table's ERCOT study profiles (2 and 12 Hz) overlap it only at 2-3 Hz and are study waveforms, not field data.
population: one at-scale training job; operator and region not stated
reverified: confirmed (Sec. III-A '0.2-3 Hz'; Fig. 1 caption DGX-H100)

evidence_note: Dallas-Fort Worth annual mean 66.6 F = 19.2 C. Period-of-record extremes: 113 F in June 1980 = 45.0 C and -8 F in February 1899 = -22.2 C.
notes: Batch 3 used the range of monthly normals (2.3 to 35.4 C), which excludes real extremes; replaced with the record extremes from the same page. Conversions: (113-32)*5/9 = 45.0; (-8-32)*5/9 = -22.2. The page lists 20.2 days per year at or above 100 F and 29.2 freeze days per year (Batch 3 said per season). Monthly normal table matched exactly.
population: DFW station 1991-2020 normals; records since 1899
reverified: confirmed (monthly table, 66.6 F, 20.2 days, records)

evidence_note: Vendor field data from over 100 commercial BESS sites showed state-of-charge errors up to 15%, with outliers above 40%. A well-calibrated LFP battery management system targets 2%.
notes: Typical is the midpoint (filled). Low 2 is a target (http://www.motor.com/2026/05/ev-battery-soc-soh-pid-accuracy/), not a measurement. Both sources are a vendor or secondary article; the author is ACCURE's battery intelligence director. Sign and basis (absolute SOC points) not specified.
population: stationary BESS fleet (vendor database); EV controllers
reverified: confirmed (+/-15%, >40% outliers, 100+ sites, ACCURE; +/-2% target)

evidence_note: Bounds derived: low = 0.70 (capacity end-point) times (1 - 0.15 SOC error) = 0.595; high 1.0 = new and accurate.
notes: Batch 3 found no direct source. This is a derived modeling range that assumes operators hold back a margin equal to the SOC error (physics-reasoned, not sourced). Typical is the midpoint of the derived bounds. The Sandia temperature curve for this node is kept as a candidate edge, not loaded.
population: derived
reverified: n/a (derived)

evidence_note: EVE 3.2 V 314 Ah LFP cell is rated for 8000 cycles at 25 C to 70% state of health; not to be used below 60% of nominal capacity. A Sandia LFP cell lost 10 to 15% capacity over 8394 partial-state-of-charge cycles.
notes: Low 0.70 is the rated test end-point, not a field value; high 1.0 is the definition of new. Typical is the midpoint (filled). The sources are in cycles, not years. P3 whitepaper defines end of life as 80% capacity.
population: one vendor LFP cell; one lab LFP cell
reverified: confirmed (EVE Table 3, Sec. 3; Sandia 10-15%; P3 80%)

unit: ratio to new at room temperature
evidence_note: P3 says internal resistance is about 5 times higher at -20 C than at room temperature (no cell type named). End of life is +33% resistance (P3) or 150% of initial (EVE). A Sandia LFP cell rose from 0.0036 to 0.0042 ohm after 8394 cycles (1.17x).
notes: Low and typical 1.0 are the definition (new cell at room temperature); Batch 3 left typical blank and a midpoint fill (3.0) would be wrong. High 5 is a cold-cell ratio and is not reachable for a conditioned room in Texas. Batch 3's 'mixed NCA/LFP cells' is not in the P3 document; removed. Sandia resistance is Cell #1 only.
population: cells at -20 C (P3); one LFP cell (Sandia)
reverified: confirmed with correction (5x yes; chemistry not named in P3)

evidence_note: Vertiv Liebert EXL S1 UPS inverter lists 110% continuous overload and up to 200% of rated current for short circuits (200% for 200 ms, or 155% for 5 s when bypass is unavailable).
notes: Typical is the midpoint (filled) of two different quantities (continuous overload rating and short-circuit limit). One vendor's UPS inverter, not a grid-forming converter. Not Texas-specific. The Vertiv 800 kW spec gives two bypass overload figures (500% for 10 cycles, and 500% for one cycle); verify with Vertiv.
population: one vendor (Vertiv) UPS family
reverified: confirmed (110% / 200% for 200 ms at 25 C; 800 kW spec)

evidence_note: Vertiv EXL S1 allows 125% overload for 10 minutes (600 s) and 150% for 60 s at 25 C.
notes: The range spans two overload LEVELS (150% and 125%) of one product, not vendor variation; treat it as a scale parameter. Typical 190 s is the geometric mean (filled), because the span is a factor of 10. The 200% / 0.2 s rating is a different regime and is kept in simulator_validation.csv as part of the overload capability curve.
population: one vendor UPS inverter
reverified: confirmed (125% 10 min, 150% 60 s, 25 C)

evidence_note: TDK/EPCOS B41694/B41794 aluminium electrolytic capacitors reach end of useful life at a capacitance change of plus or minus 30% of initial.
notes: Low 0.7 is an end-of-life limit, not an observed field value; high 1.0 is new by definition. Typical is the midpoint (filled). One capacitor series; not necessarily this product's DC link. No film-capacitor data found.
population: one manufacturer series
reverified: confirmed (change within +/-30%, ESR up to 3x)

evidence_note: SEL-751A feeder relay voltage metering is accurate to plus or minus 1% of reading (2% with the xx71xx card) for 24 to 264 V.
notes: Typical is the midpoint (filled). Basis is accuracy of reading, not of the threshold setting. One relay model. The data sheet lists no settable 27/59 delay.
population: one vendor, one relay model
reverified: confirmed (+/-1% of reading, +/-2% with card; <1.5 cycles; no 27/59 delay)

evidence_note: Advanced Energy/Artesyn 50 V 3 kW Open Rack V3 PSU lists 20 ms typical hold-up at 100% load on 200 to 277 VAC. Bel TEC3000 (3 kW) lists 10 ms at 70% load.
notes: Typical equals high because it is a single data-center-class PSU; hold-up falls with load (ORv3 table: 13.33 ms at 150%). Different products, different loads. ATX's 16-17 ms is a requirement (requirements.csv). Not Texas-specific.
population: two vendor server PSUs (3 kW)
reverified: confirmed (ORv3 20 ms; Bel 10 ms at 70% load, 11 ms at 60%)

evidence_note: A Trane RTAA air-cooled chiller trips on under-voltage when line voltage falls below a threshold set 10% from nominal. Third-party sources put the drive DC-bus under-voltage trip at about 70 to 75% of nominal.
notes: Mixes two bases: line voltage (Trane, 90%) and DC bus (VFD article, low 70%). The Trane article gives no absolute value and no time delay. The VFD article is unsigned, unaffiliated with manufacturers and cites no standards or manuals: treat the low bound as opinion-grade. Row stays opinion.
population: one chiller family (Trane RTAA 70-400 ton); generic VFDs
reverified: confirmed (Trane 10% below nominal; VFD 70-75% DC bus); VFD source is weak

page_or_table: Data Centers Rapid Restart; CGAM Anti-Recycle Timers
evidence_note: Trane RTAC: restart inhibit 120 s by default (30 to 120 s adjustable), minimum 5 minutes between starts, power-up checks 15 to 30 s, first compressor often 1 to 2 minutes after power returns. Trane CGAM: stop-to-start 10 s and start-to-start 360 s.
notes: Low (10 s) and typical (120 s) are stop-to-start inhibits; high (360 s) is a start-to-start lockout whose applicability to the first restart after power loss is not stated. Two models only. Definitions are mixed.
population: Trane RTAC and CGAM air-cooled chillers
reverified: confirmed (RTAC 120 s, 30-120, 5 min, 15-30 s; CGAM 10 s, 360 s)

evidence_note: The page describes N+1 as one module that can be offline and N+2 as any two modules out of service while the rest carry the load; 2N allows one whole group offline.
notes: Design allowances only; no measured count of modules actually offline for maintenance exists in the sources. Low 0 and high 2 follow N+1 and N+2; typical 0 is an assumption (usually nothing offline). Fleet size is a fixture to be chosen.
population: design allowance, not a measured population
reverified: confirmed (redundancy definitions); counts are assumptions

unit: fraction of rated capacity per online unit
source_type: derived from the equation with sourced cross-check
evidence_note: Derived: loading = load_fraction / (1 - units_offline / n_units) with n_units = 10 (fixture). Low = 0.2 / 1, typical = 0.5 / 1, high = 0.97 / 0.8 = 1.21. Cross-check: Active Power says UPS in mission-critical sites typically run at 30 to 80% of rated capacity; at typical load with 0 to 2 of 10 units offline the equation gives 0.50 to 0.63, inside that band.
notes: Batch 6 reported 0.3 to 0.8 (vendor design range). That band excludes the overload cases a failure hunt must reach, so the node range follows the equation. n_units = 10 is an assumption. Riello's UK sample: over half of 2,268 UPS ran below 50% load, only 3 above 75%.
population: vendor white paper (Active Power); UK service sample (Riello, 2015-16)
reverified: confirmed (Seika 30-80%, 2N 50%, N+1 66%; Riello sample)

page_or_table: Uptime Global Data Center Survey 2024 as summarized by DCD
evidence_note: Whole-facility figures only: mean age 11.3 years, capacity-weighted 10.2 years, 48% of facilities older than 10 years, design lifespan cited as 10 to 15 years.
notes: No equipment-level age data exists in the sources. Range is a modeling choice: 0 (new) to 15 years (upper end of the cited facility design lifespan); typical 7.5 is the midpoint. The survey is global and the author notes it is not representative. Batteries typically last 3 to 5 years (VRLA, APC); LFP lasts longer.
population: global facilities; not Texas; not equipment
reverified: confirmed (DCD figures); range is an assumption
